slides.texte_overlay:
How to master the art of
being able to talk to anyone
Start with the situation you share. "How do you know the host?" or "Have you tried the food yet?" A shared moment is the easiest door into any conversation, with anyone.
Ask "how" and "why" questions. Not "Do you like your job?" but "How did you end up doing that?" Open questions get people telling stories instead of giving one-word answers.
Match their energy, then lift it a little. Calm person, calm voice. Excited person, smile more. Meeting people where they are makes them feel understood from the first minute.
Find the thing they light up about. Watch their face as they talk. When it changes, ask more about that. Everyone has one topic that turns them on, your job is just to find it.
Share a small story of your own. Conversation is a trade. After a few questions, offer something back. "That reminds me of the time I..." makes it feel like a real chat, not an interview.
Before: nothing to say outside my own bubble. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and something real to connect on with almost anyone I meet, anywhere.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: nothing to say outside my own bubble. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I can connect with almost anyone.

slides.texte_overlay: End warmly and on time. "Really great talking to you, I'll let you get back to the party." Leaving on a high note makes people remember you as easy and fun to talk to.
